title.en: Mnemonic 2: Mineral Association of Rock Systems

en.title: Mnemonic 2: Mineral Association of Rock Systems
en.decryption: Quick match for exams: **Dharwar** is the primary source of **metallic minerals** (iron, manganese, gold); **Gondwana** is the primary source of **coal**.

hi.title: Mnemonic 2: Mineral Association of Rock Systems
hi.decryption: Quick match for exams: **Dharwar** is the primary source of **metallic minerals** (iron, manganese, gold); **Gondwana** is the primary source of **coal**.

fact.en: Trap 1: Fossil Presence in Archean Rocks: Archean and Dharwar rock systems are completely unfossiliferous (contain no fossils) because they formed before complex life evolved on Earth. A common trap is matching Dharwar rocks with plant fossils.
fact.hi: Trap 1: Fossil Presence in Archean Rocks: Archean and Dharwar rock systems are completely unfossiliferous (contain no fossils) because they formed before complex life evolved on Earth. A common trap is matching Dharwar rocks with plant fossils.

fact.en: Trap 2: Coal type of India: Although coal is associated with Carboniferous systems worldwide, India's Carboniferous rocks are mostly marine and lack coal. 98% of Indian coal belongs to the younger Gondwana system (Permian-Jurassic), and it is mostly non-coking bituminous coal.
fact.hi: Trap 2: Coal type of India: Although coal is associated with Carboniferous systems worldwide, India's Carboniferous rocks are mostly marine and lack coal. 98% of Indian coal belongs to the younger Gondwana system (Permian-Jurassic), and it is mostly non-coking bituminous coal.

fact.en: Trap 3: Geological Stability: The Himalayas are not stable; they are young, weak, and flexible fold mountains still rising due to ongoing plate collision (seismically active Zone V). In contrast, the Peninsular Block is one of the most stable geological shields on Earth.
fact.hi: Trap 3: Geological Stability: The Himalayas are not stable; they are young, weak, and flexible fold mountains still rising due to ongoing plate collision (seismically active Zone V). In contrast, the Peninsular Block is one of the most stable geological shields on Earth.

fact.en: Trap 4: Karewa Deposits: Karewas are lacustrine (lake-deposited) silt clays found specifically in the Kashmir valley. They are famous for **Saffron (Zafran) cultivation**, not tea or wheat.
